purpose: F-16/F-17 minimal counterexample matrix for the V2 C03 rules (G0-V2-SEMANTIC-REVIEW-001)
method: EVERY verdict in this file was derived by READING the source (registry.py, g0_criteria_v2.json, g0_judge.py at d8a0728/f679995). NOTHING WAS EXECUTED. A reviewer may mechanically confirm the 'current_judge' and the integrity_issues claims once a pure-logic execution is authorized.
doctrine_used_for_correct_verdict: FAIL needs proof that the mechanism under test violated the protocol
a violation visible among the PARSED records (positive) is proof
an ABSENCE is proof only if the registry is corroborated: parse report clean AND parsed record count == reg_memory_count AND writer_seq == reg_memory_count
otherwise (early stop, damaged or uncorroborated registry, bench I/O failure) the check is UNEVALUABLE -> BLOCKED
independent evidence (fork count, release byte written, child messages) can prove an action whose preceding record is absent, again only on a corroborated registry

counterexamples.question: Q1
counterexamples.title: duplicate FORKED, consecutive seq (completed run)
counterexamples.cause: second FORKED record written/duplicated for the same node
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation: two FORKED records for one node contradict the single-fork lifecycle (same class as duplicate INTENT/DEAD, which V2 F1 already fails)
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: no rule: F1 lists duplicates only for RUN_START/RUN_END/INTENT/DEAD; pass_when holds (integrity_issues empty; chain INTENT<FORKED<REGISTERED<RELEASED<DEAD holds for the first of each)
counterexamples.source_basis: registry.py:61-80 integrity_issues has no duplicate rule for FORKED; :146-168 fold() keeps the LAST FORKED; :218-246 check_order keeps the last seq per kind; :83-143 lifecycle_issues only DUPLICATE_INTENT/RUN_END/RECORD_AFTER_DEAD

counterexamples.question: Q1
counterexamples.title: duplicate REGISTERED with different pid, both before RELEASED (completed run)
counterexamples.cause: second REGISTERED written (e.g. a re-registration)
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation: one node cannot be registered twice with two identities
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: no rule for duplicate REGISTERED; C04/C07 read the first REGISTERED only (g0_judge.py c04/c07 use k['REGISTERED'][0])
counterexamples.source_basis: registry.py:146-168 fold keeps the last REGISTERED (pid 201); :72-77 checks only that last record's field types; :233-236 check_order compares last seqs only

counterexamples.question: Q1
counterexamples.title: duplicate RELEASED, consecutive seq (completed run)
counterexamples.cause: second RELEASED record
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation: a node is released once (observer.release requires state REGISTERED, observer.py:128-131)
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: no rule for duplicate RELEASED
counterexamples.source_basis: registry.py:233-234: s['RELEASED'] is the last seq (6) and REGISTERED(4) > 6 is false, so check_order stays silent

counterexamples.question: Q1
counterexamples.title: REGISTERED, RELEASED, then a second REGISTERED (completed run)
counterexamples.cause: late duplicate REGISTERED
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation (duplicate REGISTERED after RELEASED)
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: integrity_issues is non-empty (check_order reports 'RELEASED without earlier REGISTERED' because the LAST REGISTERED seq 6 > RELEASED seq 5), so pass_when fails; F1 'RELEASED before REGISTERED' fits only if read against the last REGISTERED. No rule names the duplicate

counterexamples.question: Q1
counterexamples.title: duplicate FORKED, early stop
counterexamples.cause: as CE-D1 but the run stopped at the READY wait
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation, independent of how the run ended
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: no F rule; U1 needs 'only missing later-lifecycle records' which is false; the sentence 'an early stop that fires no fail rule is U1 or U2' then implies BLOCKED
counterexamples.current_judge_basis: g0_judge.py:55-56 incomplete branch runs check_order only; no issue, so Uneval (:74)

counterexamples.question: Q2
counterexamples.title: REGISTERED with starttime null (completed run)
counterexamples.cause: malformed critical field
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation: the identity record is unusable (registry.py:76-77 MALFORMED_REGISTERED exists precisely because cleanup would otherwise lose the node)
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: pass_when requires integrity_issues empty, so no PASS; but none of F1-F4 names malformed FORKED/REGISTERED fields (F1's malformed clause covers only RUN_START/RUN_END). The 'exhaustive' sentence claims F1/F2/F4 fires; none does literally

counterexamples.question: Q2
counterexamples.title: REGISTERED with starttime null, early stop
counterexamples.cause: as CE-M1, run stopped at the READY wait
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: no F rule; U1 does not match (nothing missing); sentence implies BLOCKED

counterexamples.question: Q2

counterexamples.question: Q3
counterexamples.title: early stop, REGISTERED present, FORKED line lost, seq gap, counts disagree
counterexamples.cause: a clean-boundary line loss after writing (disk/tamper)
counterexamples.correct_basis: the registry is not corroborated (parsed 5 != written 6): the absence may be evidence loss, which proves nothing about the protocol
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: F2 'a gap in seq' with parse_clean (torn_tail=false, corrupt_lines=0 because the whole line vanished) -> FAIL
counterexamples.current_judge_basis: incomplete branch: check_order has no FORKED requirement (registry.py:239-240 only 'FORKED without INTENT'); integrity_issues not called
counterexamples.source_basis: registry.py:64-70 reports the gap; parse_reg (:30-58) cannot see a vanished line; observer.py:505-506 compares counts only inside verify_run_set (not run on the early-stop path)

counterexamples.question: Q3
counterexamples.title: early stop, REGISTERED present, FORKED never written, contiguous seq, counts agree
counterexamples.cause: writer skipped FORKED (a writer defect; the real writer always writes FORKED between INTENT and REGISTERED, observer.py:71,84,99,118)
counterexamples.correct_basis: corroborated hole: a later lifecycle record (REGISTERED) exists while an earlier one (FORKED) is absent and no loss is possible. Alternative defensible reading: BLOCKED, because the bench's own recovery logic (registry.py:170-183) works from REGISTERED alone and check_order has no FORKED requirement
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: no F rule (F2's predecessor list lacks REGISTERED-without-FORKED; F3 covers only records that must PRECEDE an action, FORKED is written after the fork); U1 lists FORKED as a 'later-lifecycle' record although it precedes REGISTERED
counterexamples.source_basis: observer.py:84-99 (_note_forked writes FORKED right after fork), registry.py:239-240

counterexamples.question: Q3
counterexamples.title: completed run without FORKED, contiguous seq, counts agree
counterexamples.cause: as CE-F2 but the run completed
counterexamples.correct_basis: corroborated, completed
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: F4 (required record absent, completed, parse_clean)

counterexamples.question: Q4
counterexamples.title: registry append failed (ENOSPC) for RELEASED, then RUN_END(false) written
counterexamples.cause: bench I/O failure: RegWriter.write increments seq BEFORE the append, so a failed append consumes a seq number
counterexamples.correct_basis: the gap is explained by a failed write (writer_seq 6 != 5 records), not by a protocol violation; no release byte was written
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: F2 'a gap in seq' with parse_clean (the failed append wrote nothing) -> FAIL
counterexamples.source_basis: registry.py:19-27 (seq += 1 at :23 before C.append_jsonl at :26); common.py append_jsonl raises OSError on a failed or short write

counterexamples.question: Q4
counterexamples.title: completed run, DEAD and RUN_END lines lost at the end of the file
counterexamples.cause: clean-boundary tail loss after the run
counterexamples.correct_basis: evidence loss (parsed 5 != written 7), not a protocol violation
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: F4 (completed, parse_clean, DEAD/RUN_END absent) -> FAIL
counterexamples.source_basis: registry.py:30-58 (parse cannot see a vanished tail); observer.py:505-506 would have caught it only if the loss happened before verify_run_set

counterexamples.correct_basis: not corroborated

counterexamples.question: Q4

counterexamples.cause: e.g. an exception while installing the guard
counterexamples.correct_basis: nothing happened
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: U1's list of tolerated missing records omits INTENT (and RUN_START); F3 needs fork_calls >= 1; the exhaustiveness sentence resolves it to BLOCKED

counterexamples.question: Q4

counterexamples.cause: exception before the first write
counterexamples.correct_basis: no evidence
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: readable empty file is neither 'missing' nor 'torn' (parse_reg: lines=[b''] -> torn False), so U2 does not name it; sentence resolves

counterexamples.question: Q4
counterexamples.title: RUN_END(false) without RUN_START, contiguous seq, counts agree
counterexamples.cause: writer defect (RUN_START is always the first write, g0_run.py)
counterexamples.correct_basis: corroborated hole at the head (RUN_START absent while later records exist)
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: I12/I16 (RUN_START_COUNT, RUN_END_WITHOUT_RUN_START) are not mapped by any F rule; F4 needs a completed run

counterexamples.question: Q4
counterexamples.title: child INTENT whose creator is not yet registered (early stop)
counterexamples.cause: ticket granted to an unregistered creator; unreachable in G0 (spec children=[]), listed for rule completeness (integrity issue I10)
counterexamples.correct_basis: positive violation: the second node's INTENT precedes its creator's REGISTERED record, and G0 allows exactly one node
counterexamples.v2_literal_rule: I10 (registry.py:242-246) is not mapped by any C03 rule; C11 owns the one-node budget but is UNEVALUABLE after an early stop (limitation L-1)
counterexamples.current_judge_basis: g0_judge.py:55 check_order reports 'creator n1 not registered before child INTENT'
